The game is played on a modular map representing the insect micro-world: hunting grounds, strategic areas, environmental bonuses, and a highly contested central termite mound. Each player begins with their own anthill, the core from which their colony expands. The game features 16 ant species, all fully asymmetric, each with its own rules, strengths, limitations, and playstyle. Mastering your species while understanding the behavior and threats of others is key to success. Throughout the game, players will: Deploy ants to claim hunting zones, Take advantage of environmental bonuses, Complete species-specific objectives, Adapt to the presence and pressure of rival colonies The central termite mound can become a powerful strategic asset, granting significant advantages, but it comes with a critical responsibility: feeding your population. Overexpansion or poor planning may lead to starvation and collapse. In Microlonies, every choice matters. Growth, area control, direct interaction, and resource management are tightly interwoven in a demanding game where only the most adaptive colony will prevail. [Rating: 5/10] Microlonies features an interesting mancala action selection mechanic, where the chamber and the number of ants at the last drop determine the action and its strength.   The actions let you expand your best (to get more ants), explore the surface (to get resources) and collect goal cards (to score the resources you collect).  Ufortunately, the game lacks tension and interaction. Besides the mancala, there are few restrictions and the game is more about optimizing than surviving.   I may give Microlonies another chance but can’t see why I would choose this over the better any game Myrmes.

[Rating: 7/10] Jeu expert prometteur, faire d'autres parties avant de se faire un avis Asymétrique -> problème d'équilibrage ?

[Rating: 8/10] Microlonies really has everything to make a Eurogamer’s heart beat faster.  As you’d expect from a Mancala mechanism, there are some interesting opportunities for planning your actions. We tried the game on BGA and can't stop playing!   The factions are truly distinctive, yet surprisingly well balanced. There are 16 of them in the game and it's really fun to discover and figure out how to play them. Time will tell just how good the balance is, but the game is already incredibly fun to play.   The interaction comes from moving ants around the board and racing for hunting grounds and expansion. 

[Rating: 8/10] Aesthetic: 2 Mechanism: 2 Involvement/length/fluid: 1 Replayability: 2 Other: 1 Different ant types make for another gameplay every time. Action selection makes for an interesting challenge.

[Rating: 8.5/10] A very nice game in which the mechanics fit the theme perfectly.   Pros: - The mechanics and the theme work very well together. - Downtime is very short, since you can only perform one action per turn. - The replay value is very high, as there are 16 different ant colonies.  Cons: - The game has a lot of small pieces, but the sorting options are rather poor
